Principal Components Analysis (PCA) Image Compressor

Image Compression Function

# Initialize compression function
pca_compress <- function(img_matrix, k){
  img_pca <- prcomp(img_matrix, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE) # Perform PCA on img_matrix
  scores <- img_pca$x[, 1:k] # Extract first k PC scores
  eigenvectors <- img_pca$rotation[, 1:k] # Extract first k eigenvectors
  comp_img <- scores %*% t(eigenvectors) # Obtain rank k approximation of img_matrix
  error <- norm((img_matrix - comp_img), type = "F") # Calculate error of rank k approx.
  return(list(img = comp_img, error = error))
}

Image 1

Original Image vs. Ranks 1-10 Approximation

Approximation Error

First Eigenvector

Interpretation: The weights from Image 1’s first eigenvector are relatively evenly spread out, meaning that the variables have generally balanced contributions.

First PC Score

Interpretation: The values of the first PC score are normally distributed, implying that Image 1’s data is varied evenly around its average.

Conclusion

I would argue that the rank k at which the approximation of Image 1 is “sufficiently good” is at k = 100 (the maximum value for k, though this approximation is still not visually “good”).

Image 2

Original Image vs. Ranks 1-10 Approximation

Approximation Error

First Eigenvector

Interpretation: Because the weights have a uniform distribution, the variables from Image 2 all contribute equally to the first principal component.

First PC Score

Interpretation: The values of the first PC score are normally distributed, implying that Image 2’s data is varied evenly around its average.

Conclusion

I would argue that the rank k at which the approximation of Image 2 is “sufficiently good” is at k = 1, as almost all approximations following this rank look the same.

Image 3

Original Image vs. Ranks 1-10 Approximation

Approximation Error

First Eigenvector

Interpretation: The distribution of weights from the first eigenvector for Image 3 is multimodal, implying that the variables fit into “groups” that have similar behaviors.

First PC Score

Interpretation: The distribution of values of the first PC score is multimodal, implying that Image 3’s data might be clustered in unique groups.

Conclusion

I would argue that the rank k at which the approximation of Image 3 is “sufficiently good” is around k = 30.

Image 4

Original Image vs. Ranks 1-10 Approximation

Approximation Error

First Eigenvector

Interpretation: The distribution of weights from Image 4’s first eigenvector has a large peak at the positive end, implying that there is a group of variables behaving similarly that contribute largely to the first principal component.

First PC Score

Interpretation: The values of the first PC score are almost normally distributed but have a long right tail, implying that Image 4’s data is varied evenly around its average with the exception of a subgroup of more extreme data.

Conclusion

I would argue that the rank k at which the approximation of Image 4 is “sufficiently good” is at k = 20, as almost all approximations following this rank look the same.
